review.summary: Scope: Migration 118, the changed audit context, the digest code and the identity guard. I found no new BLOCKER in this code. The fixes match their stated intent: every whole-row change is recorded and only a true no-op is skipped; provenance reads run through the definer function, so filtered zero counts can't appear; per-session any-event overlap handles changed expiry; TRUNCATE guards and the replica check are in place; and the count is a sound revision because the ledger is append-only. New local issues: 1 MAJOR (a ledger row on every progress write), 4 MINOR, 4 NIT. The existing release gates stay BLOCKED and are not waived: synchronized20 is still 7 successes / 13 failures, the full WP, producer, intake and deployment are unfinished, the separate non-owner runtime and its grants are NOT_VERIFIED, and performance/load, populated-upgrade and catalog/partial-index drift tests are NOT_VERIFIED. This is a private foundation only: it gives no positive coverage and does not enable production. The harness source wasn't supplied, so the receipt counts only as reported evidence. The prior record (6 MAJOR in the findings, 5 in its summary) should be corrected to 6.

findings.issue: The full WP is still not achieved: synchronized20 is 7 successes / 13 failures, and producer, intake and deployment work is unfinished.
findings.evidence: Stated in the request; the local receipt only covers the private ledger.
findings.impact: Release and any positive coverage claim are blocked.
findings.required_test: Synchronized20 at 20/20, plus producer, intake and deployment end-to-end tests.
findings.recommended_fix: Keep coverage at 'unknown' and collection disabled until every gate passes.

findings.issue: A separate non-owner runtime role with scoped grants is NOT_VERIFIED. If the runtime role is the owner, it can disable triggers or change DDL, so none of the immutability holds.
findings.evidence: No GRANT on the provenance function to any runtime role. Trust boundary trusts the owner. Prisma setups often share one role.
findings.impact: Immutability and provenance are only guaranteed under a role setup nobody has deployed.
findings.required_test: Deployed check: the runtime role is not the owner and lacks BYPASSRLS/superuser, holds only EXECUTE on the provenance function, and gets denied on direct DML/TRUNCATE/ALTER of ledger and source tables.
findings.recommended_fix: Add an explicit runtime grant migration and a startup assertion that current_user is not the owner.

findings.issue: Performance/load, populated-upgrade, partial-index drift and full catalog tests are still NOT_VERIFIED.
findings.evidence: Stated in the request; the receipt comes from a fresh, empty DB.
findings.impact: Upgrade behaviour and scale behaviour are unknown.
findings.required_test: Migrate a populated snapshot; load-test session progress and audit; compare the catalog/index definitions against the expected ones.
findings.recommended_fix: Keep these as explicit release prerequisites.

findings.issue: Every non-no-op session UPDATE, including progress or heartbeat updates, adds a permanent immutable row through a synchronous definer trigger. Rows only go when the version is deleted. Revision and provenance scan and group every scope row, and no index has sessionId available for the grouping.
findings.evidence: The source trigger records a 'state' row for any to_jsonb difference. per_session uses GROUP BY sessionId over the whole scope. The indexes are scope, window(kind, anchorAt) and the issued-only partial index.
findings.impact: Writes grow with progress frequency, and audit cost grows linearly with the number of events.
findings.required_test: Load test at realistic heartbeat rates: measure ledger rows per session, write latency, and provenance query time and plan as volume grows.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a (vendorId, liveId, versionId, sessionId) index, set a budget for progress write frequency, or record a coarser change class. Document retention.

findings.issue: With an empty or inverted window, the function still returns one aggregate row, with viewingRevision 0 and zero counts, even though the real revision is above zero.
findings.evidence: Aggregates without GROUP BY under WHERE window_start<window_end. The audit SQL does not itself require startAt<endAt.
findings.impact: If scope validation upstream is ever bypassed, the digest binds a false revision.
findings.required_test: Call provenance and audit with startAt=endAt and startAt>endAt. Expect an error or 'unavailable', never revision 0.
findings.recommended_fix: Raise an error on an invalid window, or compute the revision independently of the window filter.

findings.issue: API roles are revoked by a hard-coded list. Default privileges for other roles could still grant DML or TRIGGER on the ledger tables. A TRIGGER grant would let a role attach a BEFORE INSERT trigger that changes genuine rows.
findings.evidence: The DO block only covers anon, authenticated and service_role.
findings.impact: Ledger rows could be tampered with in environments that have extra default grants.
findings.required_test: After migrating, assert that relacl on both ledger tables and the sequence, and proacl on all five functions, contain only the owner.
findings.recommended_fix: Assert the ACLs in the migration, or revoke from every grantee found in pg_class.relacl.

findings.issue: The harness source wasn't supplied, so the receipt booleans can't be checked, including nonOwnerProvenanceNotFiltered and the expected 3 issued / 2 interval / 5 state counts.
findings.evidence: The receipt is reported evidence only.
findings.impact: The correctness claims rest on tests nobody has reviewed.
findings.required_test: Review the harness assertions, in particular exact event counts for progress-only updates and the non-owner role setup.
findings.recommended_fix: Supply the harness, or a test listing with its assertions, for the next review.

findings.issue: The INSERT check confirms trigger depth ≥2 and that current_user is the function owner. It does not confirm which function is calling. Any code running as the owner inside a trigger passes.
findings.evidence: The check is pg_trigger_depth()<2 OR current_user<>proowner.
findings.impact: Within the stated owner-trusted boundary, but it is weaker than a caller-identity check.
findings.required_test: Negative probe: a different owner-owned definer trigger that inserts into the ledger. Record the expected result under the trust boundary.
findings.recommended_fix: Document this explicitly, or use a dedicated owner role for these functions only.

findings.issue: The revision is defined in two places: wp20_metric_viewing_revision uses count(*), provenance uses sum(per-session events). The audit no longer calls the revision function.
findings.impact: The two definitions could drift apart, or the old function could be left as dead code.
findings.required_test: Assert the two values are equal across fixtures, or drop the unused function.
findings.recommended_fix: Keep a single source of truth.

findings.issue: context.durationMs is not in the final digest. The per-row digest would throw if any sequence or ms column comes back as a BigInt.
findings.evidence: The final digest only binds revisions, the epoch and counts. JSON.stringify is not given an explicit toString for the per-row numeric fields.
findings.impact: A changed durationMs wouldn't change the digest. A bigint column would crash the audit at runtime.
findings.required_test: Change durationMs and check the digest; check the Prisma raw types of the per-row numeric columns.
findings.recommended_fix: Bind durationMs, or note why it is excluded; stringify bigint fields explicitly.

findings.issue: The identity guard's trigger binding to Session/Interval and the existing interval UPDATE/DELETE prohibition were not supplied. Triggers also don't fire on logical subscribers or under session_replication_role=replica.
findings.evidence: Only the guard function body was shown; the negative probe is reported, not shown.
findings.impact: Session-id reuse and interval-immutability protections depend on code not reviewed here; a promoted logical replica could have an incomplete ledger.
findings.required_test: Catalog test: pg_trigger bindings and enabled state (origin/always) for the guard, interval and ledger triggers.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a catalog assertion for the trigger bindings; document that logical replication is unsupported.
